_about: Recorded footage for the Video tab and the vision models (extras/scripts/clips.py): sources (a local file or a URL with its SHA-1, the credit, the match and its two kits) and the ranges each camera loops, with an optional crop ([x, y, width, height], 0-1 of the frame). For now four SoccerTrack v2 goals (CC BY 4.0, cut by extras/scripts/footage.py), each cropped to the end of the panorama where it's scored (the organisers allow any footage in the demo pitch); M9's is also the tactical camera (the whole panorama) and the broadcast (tv, cropped), in place of the synthetic cameras; the team's own kickabout (numbered bibs, every player's consent) replaces them once filmed. The teams are named by their kits; the scores are the goals the dataset labels (its player lists name each scorer's team and number, the first kick-off frame each team's kit). Each source's labels hold the dataset's goal (in the clip's seconds, posted as a labelled play and flagged by the overlay): the panoramas defeat the pitch calibration, so the models find no goal themselves.

_candidates._about: Fallbacks if the kickabout isn't filmed: each waits for the organisers to allow real footage for auto-eventing (all match data stays synthetic). SoccerTrack v2 is in sources and cameras; the others are unused. extras/scripts/footage.py cuts clips around their goals and shots into extras/clips/footage/ (5 GB at most; SoccerNet and DFL only with --accept-terms). To use one, add it to sources (file footage/<source>/<clip>, its SHA-1 from footage/index.json, the credit, the match and kits) and a camera with its ranges.

soccertrack-v2.access: Hugging Face account, agree to share contact details; 145 GB, one file per half
soccertrack-v2.footage: 10 university matches (M1-M10), 20 halves, a fixed panoramic camera over the whole pitch (25 fps; 4096×1080, M1 3840×1906, M9 3840×1504: the ends of the pitch are small at the edges); per-frame positions and shirt-number player ids (ground truth for matchvision.numbers_eval)

soccernet.public_video: unlikely: SoccerChat's dataset card, built from it, says the videos may not be redistributed, publicly hosted or used commercially; check the NDA
